shape.name: Shape F - Productive Skills (Written Reflection)
shape.description: Midterm review and reflection lesson: students analyse exam results, reflect on strengths/weaknesses, and complete a baseline vocab/spelling test.
shape.pedagogical_justification: Feedback and reflection after assessment helps students identify gaps and set goals (Hattie & Timperley, 2007). Combining data-driven review (exam results) with a baseline diagnostic test gives students a clear picture of where they are and what to prioritise.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, learners will have reflected on their midterm performance, identified areas for improvement, and completed a baseline vocabulary and spelling diagnostic.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, learners will have reflected on their midterm performance, identified individual skill gaps, and completed a baseline vocabulary and spelling diagnostic.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
19 July, 2026
Duration:
50 minutes
CEFR Level:
A2-B1
Lesson Shape:
F (Productive Skills - Written Reflection)
Materials:
Slideshow (https://elwrush.github.io/lesson-plan-writer/m3a-midterm-review/), Listening & Reading score sheets, Baseline Vocab & Spelling Test handout, Exercise books

stages.stage_aim: To hook students with the real-world value of B2 English and activate prior knowledge
procedure: - Ask Ss to rule a fresh page in their exercise books.
- Display title slide: 'How did you go in your exams? Let's find out.'
- Elicit: Why is B2 or above important for standardised English exams?
- Ss write 3 reasons in their books (3 min).
- Check together using the B2 data slides (university, jobs, global communication, demand).

stages.stage_aim: To show overall grade averages, CEFR distribution, and skill breakdowns per class with anticipation
procedure: - Transition slide: 'Your Midterm Results.'
- Show grade overview for M3-3A: auto-animate bar chart (empty bar -> 77%). Repeat for M3-4A (70%) and M3-5A (68%). Draw attention to B1 (65%) and B2 (80%) threshold lines.
- Show CEFR distribution per class (click reveals each band segment). Ask: 'How many achieved B1 or B2?'
- Show skill breakdown (L/R/W bars) per class.
- Highlight that Reading is the weakest skill across all classes.

stages.stage_aim: To guide individual reflection on skill gaps and return graded papers
procedure: - Display reflection slide: 'Write your answers in your notebook. Which skill do we need to improve the most? How can we do it?'
- Ss write their reflection (3 min).
- Return Listening and Reading score sheets.
- Ss check their answers (3 min).
- Inform Ss that individual Writing grades will be returned later this week, but they can check with the teacher at the end of the lesson.

stages.stage_aim: To explain why vocabulary, grammar, and spelling are foundational for all skills
procedure: - Transition to 'Vocabulary, Grammar & Spelling.'
- Explain: strong vocab/grammar/spelling helps in Reading (understand more = read faster), Writing (clearer ideas), and Listening (recognise words faster).
- Inform Ss that the end-of-year finals will test all of this.

stages.stage_aim: To diagnose current vocabulary and spelling levels before end-of-year preparation
procedure: - Display the baseline test slide with timer (15:00).
- Hand out the Baseline Vocab & Spelling Test.
- Instruct Ss to write their answers clearly.
- Start the timer. Ss complete the test individually.
- Monitor and assist as needed.

stages.stage_aim: To provide immediate feedback and allow self-correction
procedure: - Display answer slides (3 sets of 8, no clickthroughs).
- Ss swap books with a partner.
- Read each answer aloud. Pause.
- Ss tick correct answers and correct wrong ones in a different colour.
- Ss count their score.
- Collect scores for teacher records.

metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, learners will have reflected on their midterm performance, identified individual skill gaps, and completed a baseline vocabulary and spelling diagnostic.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: Learners will have connected real-world B2 English requirements to their own learning goals.
